deliverables: Frontend and backend maintenance and development
Independent audits of treasury fund use and oversight metrics
Eternl Pro plan rollout for personal and company users
Eternl Core rewrite, Eternl Hub, enhanced hardware wallet support, and wallet data export improvements
request.what: Treasury withdrawal for 12 months of Eternl operations, maintenance, and improvements from August 2026 to July 2027.

claims.claim: Eternl is a non-custodial Cardano light wallet available on web, browser extension, Android, and iOS.
The proposal asks for ₳2,350,000, valued at about $0.1787 per Ada, to cover approximately $420,000 in annual costs for 12 months.
The requested budget is allocated as 55% frontend, 25% backend, 5% support, 13% admin, and 2% audits.
Eternl says it has about 100,000 browser extension installs and about 30,000 Android and iOS installs combined.
Eternl claims that about 5,500 Pro plan users, or 4.2% of its stated install base, would fully cover the annual $420,000 cost.
After withdrawal, Eternl says it will convert up to $420,000 worth of Ada into stablecoins, deposit it into a public company wallet, and return any Ada above that amount to the treasury.

The audits allocation is for independent audits of treasury fund use in February 2027 and August 2027, including receipt, custody, conversion, spending, balances, Pro plan income relevant to repayment, and refunds or repayments.
Eternl says every paid Pro plan will be recorded on-chain with metadata and that it will publish Pro plan earnings reports and repayment or donation transaction hashes.
Eternl claims 10-18% of Cardano mainnet transactions are conducted via Eternl.

Eternl states that if it does not receive treasury funds and paid licenses are insufficient beyond August, it may let developers go, reduce to essential maintenance, shift focus outside Cardano, or remove the free option.

summary: The document requests ₳2,350,000 for one year of Eternl operations under Tastenkunst GmbH, with a stated $420,000 annual cost, public wallet custody, audits, possible treasury repayment from surplus and Pro plan income, and continued wallet maintenance and feature development.
